newsitem.title: ITALY: Woody Allen unveils film for gutted Venice theatre.
newsitem.headline: Woody Allen unveils film for gutted Venice theatre.

text.p: U.S. film director Woody Allen opened the European premiere of his new film at a fundraising gala for Venice's fire-ravaged Fenice theatre but ducked out of watching his own performance on the big screen.
Allen told the audience on Tuesday night before the start of his first musical, "Everyone Says I Love You", that he never watched himself in his own productions.

"When the film begins, if you'll excuse me, I'm going to go outside. I will return at the end, so by that time if you're angry I will be here," the diminutive producer told a packed auditorium at the Palazzo del Cinema at the Venice Lido.

Speaking briefly to reporters beforehand as he left a lagoon taxi to enter the cinema with companion Soon Yi Previn, he said watching himself on screen sent him into a depression: "It makes me want to go out and take acting lessons."

Allen's first attempt at a musical has a star-spangled cast of U.S. actors including Alan Alda, Goldie Hawn, Julia Roberts and Allen himself and uses songs by Cole Porter and Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart.

Set in modern New York City, Paris and Venice, it follows the amorous exploits of a wealthy New York family, headed by Alda and Hawn, and features Allen as Hawn's luckless ex-husband and father of one of her daughters.
Allen, a frequent visitor to Venice, started fundraising for the 18th-century Fenice opera house last March after it was gutted in January by a fire now suspected to have been arson.
He had been due to play there on a tour by his New Orleans Jazz Band but was forced to shift the performance to a nearby venue and donated the proceeds to the Fenice's reconstruction.
Proceeds from the film premiere, with tickets offered at about $22, will also go to the project, which is expected to cost at least 120 billion lire ($80 million).
"I've been trying to do something for the Fenice since I was last here in Venice and I'm only glad that my picture is ready now," Allen said.

The Fenice, today shrouded in scaffolding and roofless, was opened in 1792. It burned down in 1836 but rose from the ashes like the mythical phoenix after which it is named and Verdi operas were staged there the 19th century.
Massimo Cacciari, mayor of Venice, told Reuters Television there was now no problem finding funding for the reconstruction with money coming from the state, the city and private sources.
Cacciari said building work was expected to start next summer and would last for two years.
Allen told reporters he wanted to do more for the project and had been asked to direct an opera in its aid. "I have never directed anything live in my life."
The director, who sings along with other stars in the musical, apologised for his voice.
"At home I sing fearlessly in the shower. I once thought years ago if I could give a concert at Carnegie Hall WITH the shower it would be perfect," he said.
Carnegie Hall is one of New York City's premier music venues.
